elements.text: Captain's decision to attempt a go-around late in the landing roll with insufficient runway remaining
Pilots' poor crew coordination and lack of cockpit discipline
Fatigue impairing both pilots' performance
FAA failure to require crew resource management training and standard operating procedures for Part 135 operators
Pilots were properly certificated and qualified
Airplane was properly certificated, equipped, and maintained
No evidence of preimpact structural, engine, or system failures
Airplane was within normal weight and balance limitations
The accident was not survivable
Captain allowed non-compliant cockpit atmosphere (lack of sterile cockpit, inadequate briefing, inappropriate conversation, nonstandard terminology, lack of checklist discipline)
Flight crew exhibited poor aeronautical decision-making and poor resource management
Captain failed to immediately deploy lift-dump system after touchdown
No evidence of reverted rubber or dynamic hydroplaning
Continuing the landing would have likely prevented or reduced severity
Recommendation: Establish committed-to-stop point for go-arounds
Recommendation: Require East Coast Jets to develop standard operating procedures
Recommendation: Require formalized CRM training for Part 135 operators
FAA inspector oversight could have been improved
Recommendation: Maintain consistency between training and operational checklists
Recommendation: Clearly state intended flap setting during checklists
Captain did not obtain forecast weather information
Recommendation: Obtain weather briefing from National Weather Service-certificated briefer
Recommendation: Guidance on severe thunderstorm conditions
Fatigue resulted from acute sleep loss, early start time, and possible untreated sleep disorders
First officer's use of prescription sleep aid unlikely to have degraded performance
Recommendation: Allow safe use of prescription sleep medications for occasional insomnia
Recommendation: Educate and train pilots on fatigue-related issues
Recommendation: Formal guidance on treating sleep disorders while retaining certification
Wet runway landing distances in manuals may be shorter than actual required distances on some wet, ungrooved runways
Part 135 pilot-in-command line-check requirements are not adequate
Outdated terrain database was not a factor in the accident
Recommendation: Lightweight recording system would have helped determine crew actions
